newsitem.title: CHINA: China "princelings" fail to win pass to party meet.
newsitem.headline: China "princelings" fail to win pass to party meet.

text.p: Children of three of China's most renowned communist statesmen, including a daughter of the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, have failed to win election as delegates to a crucial party congress, sources said on Friday.

Deng Nan, one of Deng Xiaoping's three daughters, failed to win election as a delegate to represent the State Science and Technology Commission at the 15th Communist Party Congress, said a source in the party.
Deng Nan is a vice minister of the commission, a position she has held since 1990.

Her failure to win a place at the congress reflected unhappiness among party members at the rise to prominence of many "princelings" -- a nickname given to the offspring of China's most senior, veteran elders, party sources said.
The rejection of several princelings was not a sign of opposition to their fathers, who still commanded widespread respect, the sources said.
Deng Xiaoping died last February, aged 92, after ruling China for nearly 20 years.

Communist Party cells throughout China have been holding internal elections to chose delegates to the party congress, which is held every five years to elect a new central committee and to set policy.

The congress is expected to be held in late September or early October. Party members who fail to become delegates stand little chance of being elected as one of about 200 full members or some 130 alternate members of the central committee.
The central committee elects the powerful Politburo and its standing committee, the most influential decision-making organisation in China.
Deng Nan was not the only princeling who failed to win a place at the congress.
Chen Yuan, vice governor of the People's Bank of China, the central bank and a son of one of Deng's closest associates, Chen Yun, also was not chosen as a delegate, a party source said.
Chen Yun, who died in 1995, had been second only to Deng Xiaoping in the party hierarchy and was one of China's most influential economic planners for more than 40 years.
Another princeling who has not elected as a delegate was Bo Xilai, mayor of the booming northeastern port city of Dalian and son of party elder Bo Yibo, the party sources said.
The younger Bo had failed to win enough votes from party members in northeastern Liaoning province to win a place on the provincial delegation to the congress, the sources said.
Bo Yibo, 89, is one of the last surviving communist party revolutionaries who swept to power with Chairman Mao Zedong when he founded the communist state in 1949.

China's top leaders are currently gathered in enclave at the northern seaside resort of Beidaihe to hammer out final personnel changes and policy shifts that will receive a stamp of approval at the congress.
